first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and two inherited findings indicate that shorter, simpler onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early activation. This is more consistent with sustainable growth than promotional pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention. Verification should confirm experiment design and whether gains extended beyond early adoption; qualified-revenue impact remains uncertain and should be measured.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening and simplifying SMB onboarding. The verified onboarding record improved completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and increased 30-day retention by 3%. The verified SMB signup simplification also lifted activation by 9% and qualified revenue by 4%, directly addressing both current declines. Measure qualified revenue and retention as guardrails because signup simplification showed a 1% retention decline and its result did not generalize beyond SMB. Avoid promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence shows material retention harm.

final2.rationale: Keep the cycle focused on shortening and simplifying SMB onboarding. Verified evidence shows improved completion, activation, qualified revenue, time-to-value, and— for the shortened onboarding flow—30-day retention. The competitor’s deeper discount increases urgency but does not reverse the known retention risk of promotional pricing, making it poorly aligned with sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Limit the experiment to SMB and monitor retention because signup simplification previously reduced it by 1% and was not validated in other segments.
